assumptions: Cardholder data = card_number, card_cvv, card_expiry, cardholder_name, per the payments endpoint input names
CVV must never be stored even encrypted, per PCI rules; PAN stored raw is forbidden per the ask
bank_account_number treated as in scope for 'can't be stored raw' because the customer said 'bank data' too
approved hosts are api.stripe.com and production.plaid.com; the sandbox Plaid host is not used in the workspace
tag pci-dss used as a label only; no PCI requirement numbers claimed
active=true and enforcement=advisory for new policies, per the skill's guidance
confusions: The skill says a policy file carries no comments but the template output and examples are unclear about whether // lines are allowed; I avoided them
No explicit guidance on whether a 'forbidden' field check should list fields that are sensitive-by-nature (CVV) versus fields the customer merely wants masked

table.field_attribute_required lists field_names+ and field_types+ both as 'at least one of'; unclear whether field_names alone is enough with forbidden true. Parse accepted it, but I cannot confirm evaluation behaviour without running evaluate
The vendor rule's providers vs hosts choice: Stripe and Plaid are not Xano provider IDs, so I used hosts; the docs say hosts or providers, so this is fine but not spelled out for SaaS vendors

The LOG-001 template limits text suggests adding datadog.log but the template only has one rule; unclear whether extending a template counts as a template change under the skill's 'start from it' rule
PCI scope: nothing in the catalogue or skill maps to PCI DSS requirements; I used tag pci-dss as a label and did not claim a requirement number
wished_for: A data-classification check or tag convention (e.g. a 'cardholder' table/field tag) so a rule can say 'fields carrying cardholder data' rather than a list of names
A PCI DSS template set mapping framework criteria to rules, with the caveat that it is not a compliance claim
A check that follows database read values into debug.log or datadog.log
An example showing a vendor allowlist for SaaS vendors (Stripe, Plaid) with hosts vs providers guidance
Clear guidance on the difference between forbidding a field in the schema and forbidding it in writes (db.add data)
why_confidence: Each policy parses cleanly, but the checks cover only part of the ask: log and storage rules are name- or reference-based, the vendor rule checks destinations not content, and nothing was evaluated (evaluate is forbidden in this run), so every finding is a prediction. The draft is a useful starting point, not a PCI control.
